organizations.normalization_notes: The wartime memorandum prints M.I.S.; the NARA OSS glossary expands MIS as Military Intelligence Service, G-2, War Department general staff. It is a military affiliation, not a civilian employer.

Dartmouth's obituary explicitly names Time, Inc. as Duke's 1937–1939 employer. The separate magazine titles Fortune, Life, and Time are editorial properties/roles and are not silently merged with the parent in source wording.
Preserve the historically named magazine; do not silently substitute a modern owner, parent, or successor organization.

The magazine is retained as the role/institution named by the source. Its relationship with Time, Inc. is noted in the Duke claim rather than replacing the source wording or double-counting a last civilian employer.

affiliations.role_title: U.S. Army lieutenant colonel; assignment from M.I.S. to OSS
affiliations.date_precision: The 1944 retrospective places his recent assignment to OSS in its September–October 1942 section; the exact transfer month and day are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: Direct 1944 memorandum says Duke was recently assigned to OSS by M.I.S. The index prints middle initial D; memorandum prints S. Box 203 should settle the discrepancy.

affiliations.role_title: associate advertising manager, Life; then advertising manager, Time
affiliations.date_precision: Dartmouth says he returned to Time, Inc. two years after joining Newsweek in 1935 and entered the Army in 1939; exact employment/commission dates are unstated.
affiliations.research_notes: A 1969 Dartmouth alumni obituary supplies the 1937–1939 employment-to-Army chronology; a BYU wartime photo inventory independently says Duke worked for Time Magazine. Time, Inc. is the civilian employer, not the immediate pre-OSS military source.

affiliations.date_precision: Dartmouth gives 1935 appointment and says he rejoined Time, Inc. two years later.
affiliations.research_notes: Earlier named media employer, not the last civilian employer before 1939 Army commission.
Fortune was a Time, Inc. magazine; this named magazine role is earlier, and is not a separate last-civilian-employer claim.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lt Col Florimond D Duke is linked with high confidence to the wartime OSS officer Florimond Duke described by the 1944 memorandum and independent institutional sources.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NARA indexes the distinctive name and lieutenant-colonel rank; a wartime OSS memorandum names Lt. Col. Florimond S. Duke in the Balkan unit. Dartmouth expands his name to Florimond DuSossoit Duke, while BYU identifies Colonel Florimond Duke as OSS personnel with a Time Magazine career.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High, not confirmed: highly distinctive full name, lieutenant-colonel rank, OSS Balkan role, and Time career align. The original NARA index has middle initial D, the wartime memorandum S; no protected identifier or Box 203 file yet resolves that discrepancy.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1944 wartime memorandum retrospectively describes 1942 OSS assignment. Dartmouth separately dates Time, Inc. employment before his 1939 Army commission; BYU's 1945 caption corroborates Time employment but is not used to date it.
claims.match_notes: Original middle initials remain D in the index and S in the memorandum; DuSossoit is a documented expanded name from Dartmouth, not a silent correction. Box 203 remains a priority.

claims.claim_text: By September–October 1942, Florimond Duke had been assigned to OSS from the U.S. Army's Military Intelligence Service (M.I.S.).
claims.evidence_excerpt: Lt.Col. Florimond S. Duke SC., who had recently been assigned to OSS by M.I.S.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The OSS section's October 1944 retrospective explicitly names M.I.S. as the sending organization for Lt. Col. Duke; the NARA OSS glossary expands the wartime abbreviation.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High: distinctive name, matching lieutenant-colonel rank, and OSS Balkan context; middle-initial conflict D/S remains unresolved.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate military predecessor in the September–October 1942 section of a 1944 wartime memorandum; exact transfer month and day are unstated.
claims.match_notes: M.I.S. is military, not Duke's civilian employer. Do not merge the 1939 Army entry and the later 1942 MIS-to-OSS transfer into one transition.

claims.claim_text: Time, Inc. is Duke's best-supported last civilian employer before he entered the U.S. Army in 1939.
claims.evidence_excerpt: he rejoined Time, Inc., two years later, serving first as associate advertising manager
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Dartmouth says he returned to Time, Inc. about 1937, held advertising-management roles at Life and Time, and volunteered for the Army in 1939. A BYU photo inventory independently records long Time Magazine employment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High: Dartmouth's expanded distinctive name, Army/OSS Balkan career, and BYU's independent OSS/Time identification bridge to the indexed lieutenant colonel; initial discrepancy still requires file review.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly bounded between his 1937 return and 1939 Army commission; no intervening civilian employer is identified, but exact cessation date is not documented.
claims.match_notes: Time, Inc. is the last documented civilian employer before Army service, not the immediate pre-OSS military affiliation; magazine roles are retained separately in source wording.

sources.locator_override: PDF page 33, item 1/8/275; employment corroboration only

claims.claim_text: Duke served as vice president of Newsweek magazine from 1935 until about 1937.
claims.evidence_excerpt: That year he became vice president of Newsweek magazine, but he rejoined Time, Inc., two years later
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Dartmouth obituary places Duke at Newsweek from 1935 until his return to Time, Inc. two years later.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High distinctive-name and wartime-role match, with unresolved D/S middle-initial discrepancy.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar affiliation, not the final civilian employer or immediate OSS predecessor.
claims.match_notes: Keep Newsweek separate from Time, Inc.; do not treat it as his final civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: From 1929 to 1935, Duke served as the first advertising manager of Fortune magazine, a Time, Inc. title.
claims.evidence_excerpt: served as the first advertising manager of Fortune magazine from 1929 to 1935
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Dartmouth obituary dates Duke's first Fortune advertising-manager role to 1929–1935, before his Newsweek and later Time, Inc. roles.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High distinctive-name and wartime-role match, with unresolved D/S middle-initial discrepancy.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented earlier prewar role; it is not the last civilian employer before Army service or the immediate military predecessor to OSS.
claims.match_notes: The magazine affiliation is distinct from the parent-company employment; do not double-count as a separate final civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Stevens Dukson in page 126 row 46 has an unresolved identity conflict; no pre-OSS employer is assigned from the current matches.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The printed index contains two separate Stevens Dukson rows; row 46's protected identifier also appears under two different indexed names on pages 123 and 234. An official Army bulk record agrees on name and identifier, but that identifier cannot be treated as unique in this index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Conflicting: printed name and Army bulk agree, yet the index repeats the protected identifier under other names. No source yet proves whether the index contains transcription errors, reused numbers, or distinct people.
claims.temporal_assessment: This is an identity-resolution warning only; the Army bulk file does not establish a pre-OSS employer or transfer chronology.
claims.match_notes: Keep rows 45 and 46 distinct. Review Box 203 and the files behind pages 123 and 234; exclude this case from default employer aggregates.

person_updates.identity_evidence: NARA prints Florimond D Duke, Lt Col, Box 203. A wartime OSS memorandum prints Lt. Col. Florimond S. Duke in the Balkan section; Dartmouth's full-name obituary and BYU's OSS/Time photo-caption inventory supply independent distinctive career context. D/S initials disagree and Box 203 is unreviewed.
person_updates.next_action: Review NARA Box 203 to resolve D/S middle-initial discrepancy and exact Army/MIS-to-OSS transfer chronology; check original employment records if refining Time, Inc. end date.

person_updates.identity_evidence: Printed page 126 row 45 has the same indexed name as row 46 but no populated protected identifier. These remain two independent source rows and person entities pending Box 203 review.
person_updates.next_action: Review NARA Box 203 for both Stevens Dukson printed rows before any merge or employer attribution; row 46's identifier is shared with other indexed names.

person_updates.identity_evidence: Page 126 row 46 and official Army bulk ordinal 5955076 agree on name and protected identifier, but that identifier is also printed under different index names on pages 123 and 234; no unique bridge or merger is warranted.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 203 alongside Boxes 196 and 379 to resolve protected-identifier reuse before accepting the Army candidate or assigning any employer.
